arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01 after a phishing campaign led to execution of a malicious PowerShell payload from Outlook. The payload deployed an unsigned DLL via rundll32.exe, establishing C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23. Initial reconnaissance from external IP 185.220.101.42 was detected scanning internal assets, though no direct link to initial access was confirmed. Full endpoint scan identified a low-severity PUP but no active malware. The incident was contained without escalation to data exfiltration or lateral movement.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 conducted Nmap SYN scan on internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Alert logged as low severity.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.
PowerShell process spawned from Outlook with encoded command, indicative of phishing payload (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe executed unsigned DLL from Temp directory (T1218.011), initiating C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001). Host file modification detected (T1565.001).
Incident response initiated following detection of suspicious process tree and network connections on WS-FIN-AP01.
Full EPP scan completed on WS-FIN-AP01; detected PUP.Optional.BrowserHelper in Chrome extension. No active C2 or malware found.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Spawned from Office Application
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
  process: outlook.exe
conditions:
  - process_name: 'powershell.exe'
  - command_line|contains: '-nop', '-w hidden', '-encodedcommand'
detection:
  selection:
    ParentProcessName: outlook.exe
    ProcessName: powershell.exe
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-nop'
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-encodedcommand'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566.001/
description: Detects encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

rule UnsignedDLL_Loaded_From_Temp_via_Rundll32 {
    meta:
        description = "Detects unsigned DLL loaded by rundll32 from user Temp directory"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        date = "2026-04-12"
    strings:
        $s1 = "rundll32.exe" fullword ascii
        $s2 = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" fullword wide
        $s3 = ".dll" fullword ascii
    condition:
        $s1 and $s2 and $s3 and not pe.signed
}

arguments.summary: A critical lateral movement incident was detected originating from external IP 45.33.32.156, which conducted a network scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). The scan triggered a low-severity alert but was not escalated. Subsequent authentication from the compromised host to the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet indicates potential lateral movement. Despite detection, containment actions (firewall block, AV quarantine, account disable) were denied due to policy and parameter issues, highlighting response workflow gaps.

timeline.description: External IP 45.33.32.156 initiated a SYN scan against 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), detected by IDS as 'ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan'. Alert severity: Low.
Successful authentication from 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101) to 10.0.1.1 using CORP\helpdesk credentials.
Incident investigation initiated. IOC lookup confirms prior scan activity. EDR shows no current malicious processes on WS-IT-101.
Containment actions (block IP, quarantine host, disable svc_backup) attempted but denied due to approval and parameter errors.
